notes: MAECI Italian Government Scholarship is a national government scholarship scheme run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (esteri.it, Scholarships/Grants section). It is not attached to any specific university, department or supervising professor; grantees enrol in Italian institutions of their own choosing. Live page https://www.esteri.it/en/opportunita/borse-di-studio returned 404 on 2026-10-14, but the official page is confirmed via the Internet Archive capture of https://www.esteri.it/en/opportunita/borse-di-studio/ : 'The section offers an overview of the scholarships/grants offered and/or promoted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation for foreign or Italian citizens.' No professor/supervisor is named on any official MAECI page.

Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is a University of Toronto undergraduate admission award (first-entry Bachelor's), automatically considered from admission and school nomination; it is not tied to any professor, lab or research programme. Official page https://future.utoronto.ca/pearson states: 'The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is the university's most prestigious award for international students' and 'The scholarship is tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry, undergraduate programs.' The only administrative contact is the Pearson Program Office in the Centre for International Experience (https://internationalexperience.utoronto.ca/global-experiences/global-scholarships/lester-b-pearson-scholarship) with an inquiry form only - no faculty email published. No supervising professor exists or is published for this award.

ARES international training scholarships are an umbrella scheme of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation (ares-ac.be): recipients enrol in a specialised bachelor's, specialised master's or continuing-education programme at institutions of their own choosing across the Federation, so no single institution, programme or supervising professor is attached to the scholarship. The live official page https://www.ares-ac.be/en/cooperation-au-developpement/bourses is JS-rendered behind a Cloudflare challenge ('Please enable JavaScript to view the page content') and archived captures are likewise JS-rendered shells; the scheme structure is nevertheless clear from the official page description and the published 2027-2032 five-year programme. No professor/supervisor is attached to the scheme.

AECID Spanish Government Scholarship (Becas Cooperacion Espanola MAEC-AECID) is a national government umbrella of sub-programmes (MASTER, COE, CULT, COOPERACION, ROMA/ROMAUE/ROMAIB, MUSICA, ESCUELA DIPLOMATICA, ASALE) run by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation. Verified on the official page https://www.aecid.es/es/becas-y-lectorados, which lists the sub-programmes ('Becas y Lectorados ... Becas Cooperacion Espanola MAEC-AECID') and gives only the AECID switchboard/generic contact (centro.informacion@aecid.es). No institution, supervising professor or faculty contact is attached to the umbrella scheme.

Australia Awards Fellowships is an Australian Government (DFAT) competitive grants programme in which an Australian host organisation (not an individual, and not a fixed university) applies for funding to host a Fellow nominated by an overseas counterpart organisation. No single institution, programme or supervising professor is attached to the scheme. Official DFAT page (verified via Internet Archive capture of 2022-03-16 of https://www.dfat.gov.au/people-to-people/australia-awards/australia-awards-fellowships) shows the scheme page 'Australia Awards Fellowships' under DFAT People-to-people > Australia Awards with grant-round details and no faculty content; live page fetch repeatedly timed out on 2026-10-14 (DFAT server slow/blocked to the fetcher).

Mekong-Australia Partnership (MAP) Scholarships are a DFAT government scheme funding additional Australia Awards Scholarships at postgraduate (Masters) level at unspecified Australian education institutions. Verified via Internet Archive capture of the official DFAT page https://www.dfat.gov.au/people-to-people/australia-awards/mekong-australia-partnership (2025-01-13): 'From 2026, MAP will fund additional Australia Awards Scholarships for Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar at postgraduate (Masters) level to undertake coursework or research in MAP thematic areas' - no named institution, programme or supervising professor; applications go through the central Online Australia Scholarships Information System (OASIS). Live page fetch timed out on 2026-10-14 (DFAT server slow/blocked to the fetcher).

Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) is a block-grant scheme: funding flows to all eligible higher education providers, each of which runs its own scholarship application/selection and supervision arrangements. Verified on the official page https://www.education.gov.au/research-block-grants/research-training-program (content via Internet Archive capture of 2026-10-01; live page fetch timed out on 2026-10-14): 'The Australian Government provides funding to eligible HEPs through the RTP to support their training of domestic and overseas students undertaking research doctorate and research masters degrees' and 'RTP scholarships are administered by individual HEPs who each have their own application and selection processes. Students need to contact HEPs directly.' No institution or supervising professor is attached to the scheme itself.
